title: Kepler sum-tone fits leave equal amplitudes possible for one fixed KIC 10001893 mode pair
abstract: We test a necessary amplitude condition for a steady instantaneous quadratic light response to published modes at 210.6816 and 196.4174 microHz in KIC 10001893. The response gives equal intrinsic sum and difference amplitudes. We fit the fixed 407.0990 and 14.2642 microHz carriers in 14 Kepler release-25 long-cadence quarters and two short-cadence months. Fits account for frame integration, local trends and the two parent modes. Early aperture data give difference and sum amplitudes of 43.45 and 7.82 ppm, but their nominal covariance radii are 20.09 and 68.47 ppm. Equal amplitudes remain possible in all 48 dependent fit variants. The short-cadence months also give no separation. Thus the small sum estimates do not reject this restricted physical explanation. Block errors have approximate coverage, and only six main noise blocks enter each short-cadence month. Other stellar modes, source confusion, frequency error and instrument response remain open. No new signal or planet is found. Code, aggregate fits, input hashes and separate-scratch retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Exposure-corrected amplitudes at the fixed sum and difference frequencies. Bars show conservative radial intervals from estimated block covariance. Their joint coverage is nominal. All paired intervals overlap.
